subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
passage: The closing bell would ring in five minutes, and Chetan's borrowed adventure book had a long tear across page forty. He pushed it behind a row of atlases on the low shelf and hurried out, hoping nobody would look. At home dinner tasted like paper. In class he kept glancing at the door as if Anjali Ma'am might walk in. On Thursday the librarian pulled the book from the shelf, found the tear, checked the card and came to Chetan's desk at recess. "This one was yours, I think?" she asked gently. His ears burned. He had carried the worry for four days, and hearing it out loud felt, oddly, lighter.

qa.q: Where did Chetan hide the book?
qa.a: He hid it behind a row of atlases on the low shelf.

qa.q: What was Chetan feeling in the days after hiding the book?
qa.a: Anxious, since dinner tasted like paper and he kept glancing at the door.

qa.q: What could Chetan have done at the shelf instead, and why?
qa.a: He could have told the librarian about the tear at once, because a torn page can be mended and the worry would have been avoided.

qa.q: How might Anjali Ma'am see the torn book and Chetan?
qa.a: As a repairable accident, since she asked gently instead of scolding, which suggests she cares more about the truth than about punishing.

grounding: A boy who tore a library book hides it behind other books, and the secret makes him anxious until the librarian asks.

subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
passage: On Tuesday, in the Class 5 library period, Omkar pulled the atlas out too fast and a page tore right across India. He looked around. The librarian, Mahima-ma'am, was stamping books at her desk. Omkar slid the atlas behind the thick dictionaries on the bottom shelf and walked out. For three days he couldn't stop thinking about it. At lunch he pushed his food around. When he passed the library, he walked faster. On Friday Mahima-ma'am stopped him at the door with the atlas in her hands. "Omkar, you had this on Tuesday. Do you know what happened to this page?" His ears went hot. "I tore it," he whispered. "I was scared." She nodded. "Next time, bring it to me. Tape is easier than hiding."

qa.q: Where did Omkar slide the atlas?
qa.a: Behind the thick dictionaries on the bottom shelf.

qa.q: How did Omkar feel during those three days?
qa.a: Anxious; he couldn't stop thinking about it and pushed his food around at lunch.

qa.q: What else could Omkar have done on Tuesday?
qa.a: Taken the atlas straight to Mahima-ma'am, so it could be taped at once.
Calmly and practically, pointing out that tape is easier than hiding.

grounding: A boy hides a library book he tore and carries an anxious secret until the librarian finds it and asks him.

subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
passage:
"Bhupen, can you come here a minute?"
"Yes, Damini-ma'am?"
"I found this storybook behind the encyclopedias. The last three pages are torn. The card says you borrowed it last."
Bhupen's hands went cold. "I... it was an accident. I tore it pulling it out of my bag."
"And then?"
"I didn't know what to do. I thought you'd fine me or stop me borrowing. So I put it behind the big books."
"How long ago?"
"Two weeks. I've been scared every library period since."
"Two weeks of being scared, for three pages." She sighed, not unkindly. "If you'd told me that day, we'd have taped it together."
"Will you stop me borrowing?"
"No. But you'll help me tape it now. And next time, you come straight to me."

qa.q: Where did Damini-ma'am find the book?
How has Bhupen felt for the last two weeks?
qa.a: Scared every library period, afraid of being fined or banned.

qa.q: What should Bhupen do next time something gets damaged?
qa.a: Go straight to the librarian that day, when it can simply be taped.

qa.q: How does Damini-ma'am see the hiding?
qa.a: With a kind sigh, pointing out that two weeks of fear was a lot for three torn pages.

grounding: A boy who hid a torn library book lives with fear for two weeks until the librarian finds it and asks him.
